Definition: Anathoth, the name of two Israelites, also of a place in Pal
BiblicalUsage: Anathoth is a town of Benjamin, a city of the priests, and the home of Jeremiah the prophet. Solomon sends the priest Abiathar there in disgrace, Isaiah names it among the towns trembling before the Assyrian advance, and Jeremiah's whole ministry begins as the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth.
TheologicalSignificance: A priestly town that produced both a disgraced priest and a faithful prophet shows me that God does not choose by address; He calls whom He will, even from a place men had written off.
